claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxygen attack during high-temperature exposure.
Oxygen attack embrittles untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Pack aluminization deposits a controlled, thin, aluminum-rich surface layer on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Subsequent oxidation of the aluminum-rich layer forms an Al2O3 surface scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale is thin, uniform, adherent, dense, and slow-growing.
Deposited aluminum diffuses toward the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Surface aluminum rapidly forms a protective alumina scale during high-temperature oxidation.
The alumina scale limits oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr.
Limiting oxygen ingress minimizes internal oxidation.
The alumina barrier preserves the alloy's bulk mechanical properties.
The alumina scale can withstand thermal cycling.
Relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, aluminized material will exhibit significantly reduced oxygen uptake after exposure near 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
Relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, aluminized material will exhibit reduced oxide-scale growth.
After oxidation exposure, aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain its high-temperature yield strength under tensile strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
After oxidation exposure, aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain its ductility under similar mechanical loading conditions.
Prolonged oxidizing exposure and thermal cycling may cause loss of alumina-scale adhesion or spallation.
Excessive aluminization temperature, duration, or pack activity may alter the bulk microstructure and mechanical performance.
